keySentence: Passepartout proved to be a truly loyal companion.

facts.Page story text 1 (draft, teacher check: Passepartout ran to catch the ship. He helped Fogg and Aouda get on board. His loyalty saved the day. Passepartout proved to be a truly loyal companion.
facts.Page story text 2 (draft, teacher check: At the port, the ship was about to leave without them. Passepartout sprinted to the dock and grabbed the ship's rope! He held on tightly so Fogg and Aouda could climb aboard. Without Passepartout's quick action, the journey would have ended. Passepartout proved to be a truly loyal companion. One person's dedication can make all the difference.
facts.Page story text 3 (draft, teacher check: As they arrived at the port, they discovered to their horror that the steamship was already departing. Without hesitation, Passepartout sprinted down the dock at full speed and leaped for the ship's railing. He grabbed the rope and held on with all his strength, creating just enough time for the others to board. This selfless act of bravery demonstrated the depth of Passepartout's loyalty to his master. Passepartout proved to be a truly loyal companion. However, Passepartout nearly fell into the churning water between the ship and the dock. Because his devotion to Fogg was stronger than his fear, he risked his own life without a second thought. Fogg silently clasped Passepartout's hand in gratitude, a rare show of emotion from the reserved gentleman.
